content:
Hi everyone. I'm not a mathematician. I'm a developer, and I've spent the past weeks building an autonomous theorem-proving and certification system with Claude Code. It picks targets, produces proofs, and accepts nothing unless the local Lean kernel certifies it. A public CI then re-checks everything.

To validate the system, I asked it to attempt something genuinely hard from Freek Wiedijk's list. It reports that it completed Morley's theorem (#84), one of the 16 still missing in Lean, and that this appears to be the first geometric formalization in Lean. I can't judge the mathematics myself, so I'm doing the only honest thing I can: publishing everything and letting the kernel, and you, be the judges.

Repository: https://github.com/Solarys431/unico-lean-proofs (file UnicoProofs/Morley.lean, tag morley-2026-07-12, CI green).

Since the mathematics is not mine, I can't answer deep technical questions, but I'll gladly relay them to the system. Below is the technical summary written by the system itself:
"In any non-degenerate triangle in ℂ (¬ Collinear ℝ {A, B, C}), any three points lying on the intersections of adjacent angle trisectors (defined as rays, via arg/3) satisfy dist P₁ P₂ = dist P₂ P₃ ∧ dist P₂ P₃ = dist P₃ P₁ (morley_classico). Companions: each pair of adjacent trisectors meets in exactly one point (∃!), and the three points are pairwise distinct. Self-contained file, ~1000 lines. Pure kernel: no sorry, no extra axioms, no native_decide; toolchain v4.32.0-rc1. Proof: Connes-style inside ℂ, with a polynomial core closed by linear_combination using exact sympy-computed cofactors, a ray-intersection lemma, an arg toolkit, and a vertex swap for the mirror case. Prior art: HOL Light (Harrison), Isabelle (Puyobro), Rocq (Guilhot), Mizar (Coghetto); in Lean, partial trigonometric identities (no points, rays or intersections) in lean-genius. If an earlier geometric Lean formalization exists, corrections are welcome."

Honestly validating this pipeline is the whole point of the experiment, so if anything is wrong, I want to know!
Happy to! Could you point me to the right place/format for it? I'll have the system prepare it.
Done! Added at the repo root: https://github.com/Solarys431/unico-lean-proofs/blob/main/formalization.yaml — thanks for the pointer, this standard is exactly in the spirit of the experiment.
On a first glance, the theorem statement looks okay. However it's stated in the complex plane, which is not general.
Also this belongs in #AI authored projects

Daniele Cappello said:

If an earlier geometric Lean formalization exists, corrections are welcome.

This problem is on https://leanprover.github.io/lean-eval-leaderboard/problems/morley_theorem, so you are not the first to formalise it. You can submit your solution by following the instructions there.
This topic was moved here from #maths > Morley's theorem (#84): AI-generated proof, please check by Anne Baanen.

Thank you Jeremy, exactly the correction I was hoping to get quickly! I've updated the repository (file header, READMEs, release notes and formalization.yaml): the claim is now "an independent geometric formalization", with a full prior-art note crediting the lean-eval benchmark. I'll look into submitting the solution there as you suggested. Thanks also for the note on generality (ℂ vs abstract Euclidean spaces), noted as future work.

Hi @Jeremy Chen , a quick update.
The benchmark submission is done and accepted (issue #780, "morley_theorem: pass").
Then, thanks to my pipeline, I tried the generalization you suggested and it worked out.
The theorem now holds in an arbitrary two dimensional real inner product space, with existence, uniqueness and non degeneracy on top.
The candidate file for Archive/Wiedijk100Theorems is here, it builds cleanly on master and the linters report nothing:
https://github.com/Solarys431/mathlib4/blob/morley-100/Archive/Wiedijk100Theorems/Morley.lean

It is ready for a PR, which will carry the LLM-generated label as the rules require. I would like to understand from you how best to proceed, and whether you would be willing to review it.
Any advice is welcome, I am here to learn.
